title: fix(plugin-gantt,plugin-calendar,app-shell): the gantt timeline, the calendar quick-create dialog and the Home and inbox relative times read the display locale (objectui#10668)
body:
Fixes #10668
Clause-②: no

Four more date faces take their locale from `useDisplayLocale()`, in the objectui#10442 shape. Two are the faces the card names. The other two came out of the census the triage asked for. Implemented by a dispatched dev subagent under seat `domain:ui#5` (session `session_01KUxVUa7e39aNjhkKi1gsoy`). The branch was cut from `f905090` and merged up to `origin/main` `383a34f52` before this PR opened.

## Measured first, on the base

The triage said to measure one face first, under an English UI with a `de-CH` display locale. All four pins below were written and run on the unmodified base before any source edit. Every leg mounts the real `I18nProvider` with an ENGLISH UI and declares the display locale through `LocalizationProvider`, so no leg depends on the runner's own locale.

- `GanttView`: the week columns read `3/2` and `3/9`, and every `toLocaleDateString` call received `'en'` (the UI language). Result: 3 failed, 1 passed (the en-US control).
- `ObjectCalendar`'s quick-create dialog read `On March 18, 2020` (this runner's machine locale), while the grid it opened from is `de-CH`. The tripwire recorded one machine-locale call. Result: 4 failed, 2 passed (the en-US control and the authored-`locale` case).
- Home rail and inbox bell: `3 days ago` at every timestamp, with `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` receiving `'en'`. Result: 6 failed, 2 passed (the two en-US controls).

The card also says `ObjectGantt`'s tooltips already read `de-CH` in the same situation. That half was not re-measured here. It is what `ObjectGantt`'s existing `useDisplayLocale()` read and its `ObjectGantt.dateLocale.test.tsx` pin already cover.

## What changed

- **`GanttView`** (`plugin-gantt`): `dateLocale` is now `useDisplayLocale()`. It was `language || undefined` from `useGanttTranslation()`. It reaches the column and band headers, the toolbar period label (`formatPeriodLabel`), the task list's dates, a bar's hover card and the readouts shown while a bar is dragged. `language` is no longer destructured there. This component has no authored `locale`, so nothing else can win.
- **`useGanttTranslation.ts`**: comment only. It said `language` is threaded into the date formatters. It now says `language` is the UI language and not a date locale. The hook still returns `language`, which `useGanttTranslation.test.tsx` pins.
- **`ObjectCalendar`** (`plugin-calendar`): the hook is read beside the component's existing `useObjectTranslation()` call. That is well away from the fetch effect, which objectui#10684 owns (the region partition). The dialog's date and time now format with `dialogLocale`, which applies the grid's own rule (`CalendarView`'s `effectiveLocale`):
  - **A set `locale` prop still wins.** It did before in the dialog, and it does in the grid.
  - When `locale` is unset, or carries the grid's `"default"` spelling, the dialog uses the display locale.
- **`HomeActionCenter`, `HomeActivity`** (`HomeRail.tsx`) and **`InboxPopover`** (`app-shell`): all five `timeAgo(…, language)` calls became `timeAgo(…, displayLocale)`. `InboxPopover` keeps `useObjectTranslation` for `t`. `HomeRail` no longer imports it.
- **`residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx`** (`i18n`): this suite asserts, as a premise, that `GanttView` takes `t` from `useGanttTranslation()`. It spelled that as the literal `const { t, language } = useGanttTranslation();`, which went red on this change (see Tests). It now uses the pattern the same suite already uses for its `useObjectTranslation` files: `t` destructured from the hook, whatever else rides along. The pattern was checked both ways. It accepts `{ t }` and `{ t, language }`, and it refuses `{ language }`, `{ tt }` and `t` taken from `useObjectTranslation`.
- **Changesets**: a `patch` for each of `@object-ui/plugin-gantt`, `@object-ui/plugin-calendar` and `@object-ui/app-shell`. The i18n test-only edit gets an empty-frontmatter declaration, per AGENTS.md, because nothing published changes there.

No new i18n key, no new or changed prop, and no export change.

### Why HomeRail and InboxPopover are in scope, and what they now render

The triage asked for every date face that does not read `useDisplayLocale()`. These two hand the UI language to `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` through `timeAgo`. The repo has already ruled relative-time faces onto the display locale: the Marketplace's (objectui#10331) and Studio home's visit times (objectui#10232). So these two now match those. The visible consequence is the same one those faces already have: under an English UI with a `de-CH` display locale, the phrase reads `vor 3 Tagen`. With no display locale declared, the display locale falls back to the UI language, so nothing changes for a tenant that has not configured one.

## Census

**Population.** Every non-test source file under `packages/plugin-*/src`, `packages/components/src`, `packages/fields/src` and `packages/app-shell/src`: 1061 files, enumerated from `git ls-tree` at `f905090`.

**First pass: date calls.** The files that call `toLocaleDateString(`, `toLocaleTimeString(`, `toLocaleString(`, `Intl.DateTimeFormat(`, `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat(`, `formatDate(`, `formatDateTime(`, `formatRelative…` or `formatTime(`: 66 files. ⚠️ My first enumeration used a wildcard pathspec and returned no `plugin-*` rows at all. The control (`ResourceWorkload.tsx` and `CalendarView.tsx` must be present) caught that, and the census was redone from `git ls-tree`.

**Three more sweeps**, for faces the first pass cannot see:

1. **The UI `language` in any argument position.** Only `GanttView`, `HomeRail` and `InboxPopover` format dates with it. Every other hit is a `pickLocalized`-style LABEL choice, which objectui#10442 excluded by name.
2. **Every component that declares an optional `locale` prop.** Only `ObjectCalendar` handed it to `Intl` unresolved.
3. **date-fns and react-day-picker faces.** These are a finding, not a fix (see the table and Acceptance notes).

Verdicts:

- **reads**: the component calls `useDisplayLocale()`.
- **fed**: a caller that already resolved `useDisplayLocale()` passes the tag in.
- **fixed**: skipped the display locale, fixed here.
- **not a date face**
- **held**: a held file. It reads the display locale, so there is nothing to file.
- **declared**: listed with its reason in `machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts`.
- **finding**: skips the display locale, but not in a shape this card can fix.

Neither sees a date face that passes the UI `language` as an expression, which is why this card's pins are per face.

## Tests

New pin files, one per fixed face. Each has a `de-CH` case, an `en-US` control, a "reading of the session, not of the machine" case that compares the two raw readings, and the `recordLocaleArguments` tripwire from `@object-ui/test-support` (no locale-taking call may receive the machine locale or `'en'`).

- `packages/plugin-gantt/src/GanttView.displayLocale-10668.test.tsx`: the week units, the month band, the toolbar period and the task list's Start and End cells. The expected strings are `2.3.`, `März 2020` and `13.3.` against `3/2`, `Mar 2020`, `March 2020` and `3/13`.
- `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.quickCreateDisplayLocale-10668.test.tsx`: clicks the grid cell named in the grid's own locale and reads the dialog's description. Only `Date` is faked, so waits run on real timers. Beyond the four common cases it also pins that an authored `locale: 'fr-FR'` still wins (`On 18 mars 2020`), and that the grid's `"default"` spelling reads the display locale.
- `packages/app-shell/src/console/home/__tests__/HomeRail.displayLocale-10668.test.tsx`: `HomeActionCenter` and `HomeActivity`.
- `packages/app-shell/src/layout/__tests__/InboxPopover.displayLocale-10668.test.tsx`: the real popover, tabs and router, with nothing mocked. It reads the single row and the group row on the Notifications tab, and the activity row on the Activity tab.

### Reverse verification

This ran after the fix and the pins were committed (on `4ab5052`), under a trap restore with absolute paths. The four source files were checked out from `f905090`.

- **On-disk proof before the run.** `grep -c useDisplayLocale` answered 0 in all four files. The defect lines counted back: 1 in `GanttView`, 1 in `ObjectCalendar`, 2 in `HomeRail`, and 2 in `InboxPopover` (that pattern skips `n.created_at`'s underscore, so it counts 2 of the 3 sites).
- **Mutated run.** 4 files failed, 13 failed and 5 passed, exit 1. The five that stay green are the four en-US controls and the calendar's authored-`locale` case, as must-not-change pins should.
- **Restore proof.** `git hash-object` equals the `HEAD` blob for all four files, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

### Gates

Every exit below was read from the command's own verdict line, captured before any pipe. Heavy runs went through `os-verify-lock`.

- **Pins on the final head `69b15589f`**: the four new files plus `residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx`. 5 files, 61 tests passed, exit 0.
- **`pnpm exec vitest run` over `packages/plugin-gantt/`, `packages/plugin-calendar/` and 19 outside files, on `8297290`.** The outside files are every test that names one of the changed source files as a path literal, plus `machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` and components' `displayLocale-9909.test.tsx`. Result: 146 files, 145 passed and 1 failed, exit 1. The one failure was `residue-namespaces-3546.test.tsx`'s premise literal described above. It was fixed in `178239800`, and the re-run on `69b15589f` is green.
- **app-shell, on `178239800`.** Every test file in the reverse-import closure of `HomeRail.tsx` and `InboxPopover.tsx` inside app-shell (85 files, computed from import, re-export, dynamic-import and `vi.mock` specifiers), unioned with `console/home/` and `layout/`, plus the residue suite. Result: 114 files, 785 tests passed, exit 0.
  - This is a declared narrowing: the other app-shell test files did not run locally, and CI runs all of them.
  - Its blind spot: a test that reads these files from disk. That half was searched for as path literals, as above.
- **`pnpm turbo run type-check --concurrency=2`** for plugin-gantt, plugin-calendar, app-shell and i18n, on `178239800`: 33 of 33 tasks, exit 0. Each package's script also runs `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, whose `include` is `src/**/*.test.ts(x)`, so the new pins are type-checked.
- **eslint, plain, on the 10 changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files** (content-identical on `178239800` and `69b15589f`): exit 0, 0 errors. `pnpm lint` is CI's. This narrowing is a measurement because:
  1. eslint's own `isPathIgnored` reports 0 of the 10 files ignored;
  2. the `--format json` output counts 10 files, 0 errors;
  3. `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService` (no type-aware linting), and no rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem, so this diff cannot move any untouched file's result.
  - Warnings on added lines: 4, all `no-explicit-any` in the calendar pin, which uses the sibling suite's `as any` idiom for the schema, data source and rows.
- **Exit 0 on `69b15589f`:** `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:self-import`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check-changeset-presence` (10 source files of 4 released packages, 4 changesets), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed` and `check-changeset-overwrite`.
  - `check:changeset-claims` is report-only. It lists six pending changesets that name a touched file: five about `ObjectCalendar`'s record source, filter, sort and config readers, and one about a Spanish pin in the residue suite. This diff touches none of those claims.
- `check:unused-deps` was not run: no dependency changed.

## Acceptance notes

- **Finding, handed to the seat to file:**
  - **The date-fns and react-day-picker faces render en-US under every display locale and every UI language.** They are: `DatePicker`'s label (`format(date, "PPP")`), the form date-picker renderer (`format(value, schema.format` or `'PPP')`), and every react-day-picker `Calendar` mounted without a `locale` (the form calendar renderer, both date pickers, `CalendarView`'s header popover and `DashboardFilterBar`).
  - **Why they are not fixed here.** They take a date-fns `Locale` object, not a BCP-47 tag, and `useDisplayLocale.ts` says there is deliberately no mapping table. The form renderer's `schema.format` is also a date-fns pattern. So the objectui#10442 shape does not apply mechanically, and a fix needs a decision.
- **Comments left stale, outside this diff:**
  - The `resolveAuthoredLocale` doc comment in `calendar-view-renderer.tsx` says `CalendarView` falls back to the ambient i18n language. It has read the display locale since objectui#10442.
  - The `createSafeTranslation` comment in `useSafeTranslation.ts` names data-table and gantt as consumers that localize dates with `language`. Neither does now, and gantt never went through `createSafeTranslation`.
- **Observation:** `plugin-report`'s `formatValue` prints dates as a fixed `yyyy-MM-dd` and reads no locale. That is locale-free by design, not this card's class.
- `useGanttTranslation` still returns `language`, and no gantt component reads it now. It is kept, because `useGanttTranslation.test.tsx` pins it and it is not this card's concern.
